items.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023
items.q: Conte Candoli, Pete Candoli, John Audino, Ray Trisceri, Uan Rasey, Jimmy Zito, just so many players that I worked with all the time

ctx.x: I was just going to say what did you learn from sitting next to those older fellas in the big band situation? Just — beyond — not only the playing of the music but just an observation of how they behaved?

Well you know what? Well sitting next to Snooky, sitting next to Sweets, sitting next to I mean I could go down the line you know, Conte Candoli, Pete Candoli, John Audino, Ray Trisceri, Uan Rasey, Jimmy Zito, just so many players that I worked with all the time that I mean I’m talking about a daily basis I’d work with these people. And what I learned from them was well first of all they were very relaxed and they did not — they weren’t uptight at all. You know there were a few people that were and I won’t…

items.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: And it was Chuck Findley and Bob Findley, brothers, and Conte and I, we went over there with the Metropole

ctx.x: Nowadays people pay for it themselves.

Yeah. Either that or a special deal of some kind or something. And you know now we did, with the Metropole Orchestra, we opened up the Trumpet Guild, I think it was the fifth Trumpet Guild or Brass Trumpet Guild they call it, in Holland. And in there they had trumpet players from South America, Maurice Andre of France that performed with the Philharmonic, and I got to meet Timofei Dokshizer, the great Russian trumpet player. And it was Chuck Findley and Bob Findley, brothers, and Conte and I, we went over there…
Wow. Well this has been really quite fascinating.
